whatIs.title: What are Parent Pay & Child Allowance?
whatIs.description: Cash benefits provided by the Korean government to families raising children. Includes Parent Pay (₩1M/month for age 0, ₩500K/month for age 1), Child Allowance (₩100K/month for ages 0-8 in 2026, plus ₩5K-20K outside the capital region and in depopulating areas), and Childcare Allowance (for home care). A First Meeting Voucher (₩2M for a first child, ₩3M from the second) is also given at birth.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Select your child's birth year and month
Add more children with the 'Add Child' button
Select daycare attendance (childcare allowance vs daycare fee)
Click 'Calculate Benefits' to see monthly and yearly amounts
Check the age timeline for what a child born this year receives up to age 12 (child allowance expansion schedule applied)

tips.title: Useful Tips
items: While receiving Parent Pay (ages 0-1) you do not get a separate Childcare Allowance. With daycare, only Parent Pay minus the daycare fee is paid in cash
Child Allowance is universal — all families qualify regardless of income
Use the 'Happy Birth One-Stop Service' at birth registration for convenient batch application
Daycare attendees get fee support instead of childcare allowance
The First Meeting Voucher must be used within 2 years of birth (children born from 2024)

items.q: How long does child allowance last?
items.a: From 2026, until the month before the child turns 9 (108 months), paid monthly. The age limit rises by one year each year to under 13 by 2030.
